Slice: Reinstate Neighbor

Intent

Let the shed manager lift a neighbor's suspension, so the neighbor can borrow again with a clean late-return record.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager, from the Suspended Neighbors screen, for a neighbor listed there. A suspension never lifts by itself after a set time.

Command / Input

Command: Reinstate Neighbor

A NeighborId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor to reinstate. Must be a registered account (INV-REI-8) that isn't closed (INV-REI-2).

There is no reason or note field: nothing is recorded about why. The command carries no "from" status: a late copy of an older request counts as a new request.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Suspended Neighbors @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Reinstated → context Neighbors Read by: Suspended Neighbors (the neighbor drops off), Neighbors and My Account (status active), and Neighbors To Flag (the late-return count starts again). Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor read it to know the suspension has lifted.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command.
reinstatedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

The event never changes. A later Neighbor Suspended suspends the neighbor again.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Reinstated feeds Suspended Neighbors, Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag, each specified in its own doc and eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

A reinstated neighbor is active again: they can check out tools, extend loans, place holds, collect set-aside tools and change their email, each under that slice's usual rules. A neighbor can be reinstated while they still have an overdue loan; the overdue loan goes on blocking checkouts and pickups until the tool is returned (INV-CHK-5, Check Out Tool). Holds they kept while suspended carry on from their place in the queue. Reinstatement starts the neighbor's late-return count again from zero: late returns from before it never count toward a later flag (INV-NTF-5, Neighbors To Flag; INV-FLG-5, Flag Neighbor). The neighbor isn't emailed; My Account shows them as active again. Suspended Neighbors, Neighbors and My Account own how a reinstatement is shown.

  • INV-REI-1: Only the shed manager reinstates a neighbor.
    • How the shed manager is recognised is the open identity question below.
  • INV-REI-2: Only a suspended neighbor can be reinstated.
    • A neighbor whose account is closed can't be reinstated, because closed is final, even if they were suspended when they closed it.
    • Reinstating a neighbor who is already active changes nothing (INV-REI-7).
  • INV-REI-7: Reinstating a neighbor who is already active succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second reinstatement.
  • INV-REI-8: The neighbor must be a registered account.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-REI-1, INV-REI-2)
    • Given: Ana (N1) is suspended and listed on Suspended Neighbors. She has two late returns within the last 90 days, a hold waiting at position 2 on the cordless drill, and an overdue ladder loan.
    • When: the shed manager reinstates N1 from Suspended Neighbors
    • Then: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for N1, with the time it was recorded. Nothing else is recorded: her hold and her loan are untouched.
  • Already active (INV-REI-7)
    • Given: N1 was reinstated and is active
    • When: the shed manager reinstates N1 again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Never suspended (INV-REI-7)
    • Given: Ben (N2) has never been suspended
    • When: the shed manager asks to reinstate N2
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing is recorded.
  • A late copy after a new suspension (INV-REI-2)
    • Given: the shed manager reinstated N1, and later suspended her again
    • When: a delayed copy of the earlier Reinstate Neighbor request for N1 arrives
    • Then: it counts as a new request: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for N1 again.
  • Closed while suspended (INV-REI-2)
    • Given: N3 was suspended and then closed their account
    • When: the shed manager tries to reinstate N3
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager (INV-REI-1)
    • Given: N1 is suspended
    • When: a request that doesn't come from the shed manager asks to reinstate N1
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can reinstate neighbors." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-REI-8)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: the shed manager asks to reinstate N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the Suspended Neighbors screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-shed-manager (INV-REI-1): who is asking is settled before anything else.
  2. neighbor-not-found (INV-REI-8).
  3. If the neighbor's status is already active, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-REI-7). Status is tested with closed first: an account closed while suspended has status closed, so it gets account-closed.
  4. account-closed (INV-REI-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can reinstate neighbors. INV-REI-1
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-REI-8
account-closed This account is closed. INV-REI-2

The names mean the same conditions as in Suspend Neighbor. neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen, which offers Reinstate only on listed neighbors. A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: reinstatement sets a state, and the command carries no "from" status. A request whose effect has already happened (the neighbor is active) succeeds and records nothing. A late copy of an older request that arrives after a new suspension reinstates again.

Requests at the same moment: Reinstate Neighbor is decided against the neighbor's events as already recorded, one at a time per neighbor. A suspension or closure landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Nothing is emailed.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may reinstate a neighbor (INV-REI-1). How the shed manager is recognised is the open identity question below.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Reinstated links a neighbor to a reinstatement. It holds no name, email or reason.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (this slice): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These match slices/register-neighbor.md and slices/suspend-neighbor.md. Close Account is specified in a slice not yet written in depth; it is checked against this key when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Suspended Neighbors, Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag. Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor treat the neighbor as active again.

Open Questions

  • Identity: how the system recognises the shed manager (brief 10 A1). This slice follows its answer; see the identity question in Add Tool.
